facts.value: Scientific cosmology can be defined as the science of the universe as a whole.
A common definition of the world/universe is 'the totality of all space and time; all that is, has been, and will be.'
There are two other aspects to the universe besides spacetime: forms of energy or matter, like stars and particles, and laws of nature.
The theory of relativity plays a central role in modern cosmology and its conception of space and time.
Space and time are conceived not as distinct dimensions but as a single four-dimensional manifold called spacetime.
Special relativity relates to the Minkowski metric, which includes both spatial and temporal components in its definition of distance.
General relativity integrates the concept of mass into the concept of spacetime as its curvature.
Quantum cosmology uses a classical notion of spacetime and conceives the whole world as one big wave function expressing the probability of finding particles in a given location.
